vienna-city-flats.name: Vienna city-owned and co-op rental housing
vienna-city-flats.outcome: About 220,000 city-owned flats and 200,000 co-operative flats; eligibility needs two years' residence and income under a limit
vienna-city-flats.limits: City's own figures; the page does not give rents or waiting times; counts differ slightly across sources.
vienna-city-flats.locator: "about 220,000 city-owned flats and 200,000 co-operative flats in Vienna"

vienna-waits.name: Datawrapper explainer on Vienna's low rents
vienna-waits.outcome: Typical 80 m2 flat 500-600 euros a month; newcomers can wait years; flats can pass to relatives
vienna-waits.limits: Blog explainer, not an official source; its 60% housing-stock figure conflicts with the city's own counts, so only the limits are used.
vienna-waits.locator: Newcomers "might have to wait years" for a low-rent flat

champlain-equity.name: Champlain Housing Trust shared-equity evaluation (Davis & Stokes 2009)
champlain-equity.outcome: One of the oldest community land trusts in the nation; homes affordable to households under 54% of area median income; average equity gain on resale $12,000; $2.1M of subsidy retained
champlain-equity.limits: Evaluation of homeownership, not rentals; one long-established trust in one region.
champlain-equity.locator: Champlain described as "one of the oldest CLTs in the nation"

clt-count.name: Community land trusts in the US
clt-count.outcome: 308 community land trusts in 48 states, DC and Puerto Rico (2024 survey); Burlington Community Land Trust founded 1984
clt-count.limits: Survey count via Wikipedia citing the Lincoln Institute; size and focus vary widely.

kc-bill-of-rights.name: Kansas City tenants' bill of rights
kc-bill-of-rights.outcome: Council approved in December 2019 with Mayor Quinton Lucas's backing; the ordinance was primarily the work of KC Tenants, a group that didn't exist at the beginning of 2019; it bars rejecting applicants solely for past evictions, requires 24 hours' notice before entry, and affirms the right to organize
kc-bill-of-rights.limits: Covers rights and conduct, not rent levels; Missouri state law limits what cities can do.
kc-bill-of-rights.locator: "an upstart group of activists and tenants that didn't even exist at the beginning of 2019"

kc-tenants-strike.name: KC Tenants union and the Independence Towers rent strike
kc-tenants-strike.outcome: Tenant union founded in 2019 with more than 10,000 members; eight-month strike at Independence Towers won flat rents, removal of junk fees and a repair deadline
kc-tenants-strike.limits: Union-reported outcomes in a magazine profile; strikes carry eviction risk and depend on strong participation.
kc-tenants-strike.locator: "a tenant union founded in 2019 that now boasts a membership of more than 10,000"

parkdale-strike.name: Parkdale rent strike
parkdale-strike.outcome: Over 300 tenants in 12 buildings struck for three months and reached a deal with the landlord
parkdale-strike.limits: Summary on Wikipedia; terms of the deal not detailed there.

cfpb-renthelp.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rent help page
cfpb-renthelp.outcome: Points renters to local rental assistance, 211, HUD-approved housing counselors, year-round utility help through the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) or the National Energy Assistance Referral Hotline, and housing choice vouchers (also known as Section 8), which cover all or part of rent for privately owned housing
cfpb-renthelp.limits: A directory, not money; assistance funds can take several weeks to arrive.
cfpb-renthelp.locator: "State, tribal, and local organizations distribute money to help renters"

nesterly.name: Nesterly home sharing
nesterly.place: Greater Boston, Central Ohio, Maine, Nashville and other regions
nesterly.outcome: Matches hosts with guests for stays over a month; guests can help around the house for lower rent
nesterly.limits: Only in listed regions; sharing a home with a stranger is not for everyone.

justfix-tools.name: JustFix tenant tools
justfix-tools.outcome: Free certified-mail repair letters, Who Owns What landlord lookup, and rent history requests
justfix-tools.limits: Mostly New York City; rent history only matters where rent stabilization applies.

apartment-list-data.name: Apartment List rent estimates
apartment-list-data.outcome: Monthly median rent for new leases at national, state, metro, county and city level since January 2017
apartment-list-data.limits: Covers new leases, not what existing tenants pay; a private company's estimates.
apartment-list-data.locator: "monthly estimates of the median rent paid for new leases"

oregon-cap.name: Oregon statewide rent cap (2019)
oregon-cap.outcome: First statewide rent cap: increases limited to inflation plus 7% a year; new buildings exempt for 15 years; rents reset between tenants
oregon-cap.limits: A high cap that mainly stops extreme increases; cities may not add their own rent control.

sf-rent-control-study.name: San Francisco rent control study (Diamond et al. 2019)
sf-rent-control-study.outcome: After 1994 expansion, landlords took about 30% of covered units off the rental market; citywide supply fell about 15% and rents rose about 7%
sf-rent-control-study.limits: One city and one expansion; other studies (NYU Furman Center 2016, Columbia 2021) found stability benefits.
sf-rent-control-study.locator: San Francisco study section; citywide rents rose about 7%

minneapolis-2040.name: Minneapolis zoning reforms and the 2040 Plan
minneapolis-2040.outcome: 2017-2022: housing stock up about 12%, rents up about 1%, while the rest of Minnesota added 4% and saw rents rise 14% (Pew via Axios)
minneapolis-2040.limits: Seen in search summaries only (Pew and Axios blocked access); most new homes were large apartment buildings; many factors affect rent.

minneapolis-zoning.name: Minneapolis ends single-family-only zoning
minneapolis-zoning.outcome: First major US city to end single-family zoning; up to three homes on any residential lot and denser housing along transit
minneapolis-zoning.limits: Page reports goals, not measured rent effects; Pew's rent figures were seen only in search summaries.
minneapolis-zoning.locator: "first major city in the US to end single-family zoning"

st-paul-cap.name: St. Paul rent stabilization
st-paul-cap.outcome: Voters approved a 3% annual cap in 2021; the city later added a 20-year exemption for new housing and further rollbacks
st-paul-cap.limits: News report; officials cited falling permits, but the page gives no figures, and the cause of the slowdown is disputed.
st-paul-cap.locator: "approved a 3% cap on annual rent increases"

nyc-right-to-counsel.name: New York City right to counsel in eviction cases
nyc-right-to-counsel.outcome: First such law in the US; city reported 84% of tenants with representation in court in 2023 stayed housed; in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024 only 42% of people facing eviction in the city received full legal representation
nyc-right-to-counsel.limits: Represented and unrepresented tenants differ, so 84% is not a controlled comparison; lawyer shortages are serious.

kc-right-to-counsel.name: Kansas City right to counsel for tenants
kc-right-to-counsel.outcome: City council resolution in June 2022 ensured tenants free legal counsel for housing issues; KC Tenants helped lead the push
kc-right-to-counsel.limits: Page does not state who qualifies; KC Tenants' role is from the St. Louis Magazine profile.
kc-right-to-counsel.locator: "ensured tenants free legal counsel for housing issues"
